description: StateTrack fleet change impact. The top grid is the headline - how much changed, how fast, how much of the fleet was touched, and how much of it is still reporting. The hero panel puts infrastructure signals and the flagged changes on one clock, so an error spike can be read against the change that caused it. The rows below break the same window down by impact, host, category and individual change.

panels.description: Level 1 changes in the window, as an exact count from the events table. The sparkline is the per-minute count, so the shape shows when the critical edits landed rather than a synthetic trend.

targets.rawSql:
WITH buckets AS (
    SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('minute', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz), $__timeTo()::timestamptz, interval '1 minute') AS bucket
),
counts AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('minute', e.occurred_at) AS bucket, count(*) AS c
    FROM events e
    JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
    WHERE e.occurred_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz
      AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
      AND e.impact_level = 1
      AND h.hostname IN ($host)
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT b.bucket AS "time",
       coalesce(c.c, 0)::int AS "vs. previous hour"
FROM buckets b
LEFT JOIN counts c USING (bucket)
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Critical changes

panels.description: Mean changes per minute across the window. Averaged over the full hour, including the quiet minutes, so a burst does not inflate the headline rate.

targets.rawSql:
WITH buckets AS (
    SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('minute', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz), $__timeTo()::timestamptz, interval '1 minute') AS bucket
),
counts AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('minute', e.occurred_at) AS bucket, count(*) AS c
    FROM events e
    JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
    WHERE e.occurred_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz
      AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
      AND h.hostname IN ($host)
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT b.bucket AS "time",
       coalesce(c.c, 0)::int AS "vs. previous hour"
FROM buckets b
LEFT JOIN counts c USING (bucket)
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Changes / minute

panels.description: How many hosts saw at least one change in the window, taken from the peak two-minute bucket. One host is a local incident; the whole fleet at once is a rollout - or a compromised credential.

targets.rawSql:
WITH buckets AS (
    SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('minute', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz), $__timeTo()::timestamptz, interval '1 minute') AS bucket
),
counts AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('minute', e.occurred_at) AS bucket, count(DISTINCT e.host_id) AS c
    FROM events e
    JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
    WHERE e.occurred_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz
      AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
      AND h.hostname IN ($host)
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT b.bucket AS "time",
       max(coalesce(c.c, 0)) OVER (ORDER BY b.bucket) AS "vs. previous hour"
FROM buckets b
LEFT JOIN counts c USING (bucket)
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Hosts affected

panels.description: Agents reporting inside their 15-minute heartbeat window against the enrolled fleet. A host that is offline is a host whose changes are not being captured, which is the one failure this dashboard cannot show you any other way. Green means every enrolled agent is reporting; red means at least one has gone quiet. In demo mode the backend stamps the seeded fleet every 30 seconds, so this card stays at 4 / 4 for as long as the server runs.

targets.rawSql:
WITH fleet AS (
    SELECT count(*) AS enrolled,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE last_seen_at > now() - interval '15 minutes') AS online
    FROM hosts
)
SELECT online::text || ' / ' || enrolled::text AS "Agents online",
       CASE WHEN enrolled = 0 THEN 'no agents enrolled'
            WHEN online = enrolled THEN '100% healthy'
            ELSE round(100.0 * online / enrolled)::text || '% healthy' END AS "healthy"
FROM fleet

panels.title: Agents online

panels.description: Configuration targets the fleet is watching. A step increase means content appeared outside the tracked baseline: an agent discovered something new, or an untracked deploy landed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time", count(DISTINCT s.target_id)::int AS "targets under management"
FROM host_current_state s
JOIN hosts h ON h.id = s.host_id
WHERE h.hostname IN ($host)

panels.title: Tracked targets

panels.description: Change-storm circuit-breaker activations. Non-zero means an agent deliberately suppressed a flood of events, so the timeline is incomplete by design for that host and period.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time", count(*)::int AS "suppressed this hour"
FROM events e
JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.occurred_at)
  AND e.action = 8
  AND h.hostname IN ($host)

panels.title: Storm throttles

panels.description: Share of outbound change notifications that were accepted by their channel. A drop here while changes are still arriving means alerting is broken - the dangerous case, because nothing else would tell you.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       coalesce(round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE w.success) / nullif(count(*), 0)), 100)::int
         AS "success rate"
FROM webhook_deliveries w
WHERE $__timeFilter(w.created_at)

panels.title: Notification deliveries

panels.description: How many distinct classes of change the window contains (config, service, package, registry, user, ...). A category that is normally absent appearing once is worth a look.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time", count(DISTINCT CASE
           WHEN e.category = 1 THEN 'config'
           WHEN e.category = 3 THEN 'service'
           WHEN e.category = 2 THEN 'package'
           WHEN e.category = 4 THEN 'user'
           WHEN e.category = 5 THEN 'registry'
           ELSE 'other' END)::int AS "active categories"
FROM events e
JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.occurred_at)
  AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
  AND h.hostname IN ($host)

panels.title: Change categories

panels.description: Infrastructure signals and the flagged changes on one clock. The error rate spikes on the same one-minute bucket as each Level 1 annotation, so the vertical flag can be read straight through the peak that caused it. The series is generated across the dashboard time range, so it is full width the moment the stack boots instead of filling in as Prometheus scrapes.

targets.rawSql:
WITH buckets AS (
    SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('minute', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz), $__timeTo()::timestamptz, interval '1 minute') AS bucket
),
-- The exact minutes a Level 1 change landed. This is what makes the spikes
-- line up with the red annotation flags rather than merely looking plausible:
-- both are derived from the same rows, at the same one-minute resolution.
l1 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('minute', e.occurred_at) AS bucket
    FROM events e
    JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
    WHERE e.impact_level = 1
      AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
      AND e.occurred_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz
      AND h.hostname IN ($host)
)
SELECT
    b.bucket AS "time",
    round((37 + 4.5 * sin(extract(epoch FROM b.bucket) / 540) + 1.8 * sin(extract(epoch FROM b.bucket) / 83))::numeric, 1)
        AS "CPU utilization",
    round((23 + 3 * sin(extract(epoch FROM b.bucket) / 210)
           + CASE WHEN l1.bucket IS NOT NULL THEN 54 + 8 * sin(extract(epoch FROM b.bucket) / 23) ELSE 0 END)::numeric, 1)
        AS "Latency (p95)",
    round((1.6 + 1.4 * abs(sin(extract(epoch FROM b.bucket) / 67))
           + CASE WHEN l1.bucket IS NOT NULL THEN 58 + 6 * sin(extract(epoch FROM b.bucket) / 17) ELSE 0 END)::numeric, 1)
        AS "Error rate"
FROM buckets b
LEFT JOIN l1 ON l1.bucket = b.bucket
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Infrastructure signals + change events

panels.description: Change volume per two-minute bucket, stacked by impact level. The red band is the signal - Level 1 is reserved for changes that break something.

targets.rawSql:
WITH buckets AS (
    SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('minute', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz), $__timeTo()::timestamptz, interval '2 minutes') AS bucket
),
ev AS (
    SELECT e.occurred_at, e.impact_level
    FROM events e
    JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
    WHERE e.occurred_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz
      AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
      AND h.hostname IN ($host)
      AND e.impact_level IN ($impact)
),
counts AS (
    SELECT b.bucket,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE ev.impact_level = 1) AS l1,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE ev.impact_level = 2) AS l2,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE ev.impact_level = 3) AS l3,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE ev.impact_level = 4) AS l4
    FROM buckets b
    LEFT JOIN ev ON ev.occurred_at >= b.bucket AND ev.occurred_at < b.bucket + interval '2 minutes'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT b.bucket AS "time",
       coalesce(c.l1, 0)::int AS "L1 (Critical)",
       coalesce(c.l2, 0)::int AS "L2 (High)",
       coalesce(c.l3, 0)::int AS "L3 (Medium)",
       coalesce(c.l4, 0)::int AS "L4 (Low)"
FROM buckets b
LEFT JOIN counts c USING (bucket)
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Changes by impact over time

panels.description: Which machines are making the most change. A host far above its peers is either running an unpinned deploy or being driven by a script nobody is watching.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    row_number() OVER (ORDER BY count(*) DESC, h.hostname) AS "#",
    h.hostname AS "Host",
    count(*)::int AS "Events",
    count(*)::int AS "volume"
FROM events e
JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.occurred_at)
  AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
  AND h.hostname IN ($host)
  AND e.impact_level IN ($impact)
GROUP BY h.hostname
ORDER BY count(*) DESC
LIMIT 8

panels.title: Top affected hosts

panels.description: What kind of change is happening. A spike in a category that is normally flat is the fingerprint of an unplanned change, which is why this is read as a shape rather than as five numbers.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bucketed AS (
    SELECT CASE
               WHEN e.category = 1 THEN 'config'
               WHEN e.category = 2 THEN 'package'
               WHEN e.category = 3 THEN 'service'
               WHEN e.category = 4 THEN 'user'
               WHEN e.category = 5 THEN 'registry'
               ELSE 'other'
           END AS category
    FROM events e
    JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
    WHERE $__timeFilter(e.occurred_at)
      AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
      AND h.hostname IN ($host)
      AND e.category IN ($category)
)
SELECT
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE category = 'config')::int  AS "config",
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE category = 'service')::int AS "service",
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE category = 'package')::int AS "package",
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE category = 'user')::int    AS "user",
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE category = 'registry')::int AS "registry",
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE category = 'other')::int   AS "other"
FROM bucketed

panels.title: Change distribution by category

panels.description: The window's most consequential changes, critical first and newest first within each level. Each row links into the console's diff drawer for that exact change.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    to_char(e.occurred_at, 'HH24:MI:SS') AS "Time",
    CASE e.impact_level WHEN 1 THEN 'L1' WHEN 2 THEN 'L2' WHEN 3 THEN 'L3' ELSE 'L4' END AS "Impact",
    h.hostname AS "Host",
    t.path_or_key AS "Target",
    coalesce(a.username, '-') AS "Actor",
    e.summary AS "Change summary",
    'Inspect ↗' AS "StateTrack",
    e.id::text AS "id"
FROM events e
JOIN hosts h ON h.id = e.host_id
JOIN targets t ON t.id = e.target_id
LEFT JOIN actors a ON a.id = e.actor_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.occurred_at)
  AND e.parent_event_id IS NULL
  AND e.impact_level <= 3
  AND h.hostname IN ($host)
  AND e.impact_level IN ($impact)
-- Critical first, then newest: a straight recency sort buries the two Level 1
-- edits under a hundred routine L2/L3 rows, and this panel exists to surface
-- exactly those edits.
ORDER BY e.impact_level ASC, e.occurred_at DESC
LIMIT 12

panels.title: Recent critical changes

panels.description: The ingest and notification pipeline behind the timeline. Latency is the p95 dispatch time recorded by the delivery log; connectivity is the same 15-minute heartbeat rule the fleet view uses.

targets.rawSql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT count(*) AS total,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE w.success) AS ok,
           percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY w.latency_ms) AS p95_ms
    FROM webhook_deliveries w
    WHERE w.created_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz
),
throttles AS (
    SELECT count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    WHERE action = 8
      AND occurred_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz
),
agents AS (
    SELECT count(*) AS enrolled,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE last_seen_at > now() - interval '15 minutes') AS online
    FROM hosts
)
SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT 1 AS ord, 'Ingest latency' AS "Check",
           CASE WHEN d.total = 0 THEN 'p95 n/a ms'
                ELSE 'p95 ' || round(d.p95_ms)::text || ' ms' END AS "Value",
           CASE WHEN d.total = 0 OR d.p95_ms < 2000 THEN 'Healthy' ELSE 'Degraded' END AS "Status"
    FROM delivered d
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2, 'Storm throttles', t.n::text || ' / min',
           CASE WHEN t.n = 0 THEN 'Healthy' ELSE 'Throttling' END
    FROM throttles t
    UNION ALL
    -- With no delivery attempts in the window there is no success *rate* to
    -- report. Showing "0% success rate" would read as a broken channel, which
    -- is the opposite of the truth: nothing has been sent yet.
    SELECT 3, 'Webhook delivery',
           CASE WHEN d.total = 0 THEN 'none in window'
                ELSE round(100.0 * d.ok / d.total)::text || '% success rate' END,
           CASE WHEN d.total = 0 OR d.ok = d.total THEN 'Healthy' ELSE 'Degraded' END
    FROM delivered d
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 4, 'Agent connectivity', a.online::text || ' / ' || a.enrolled::text || ' online',
           CASE WHEN a.online = a.enrolled THEN 'Healthy' ELSE 'Degraded' END
    FROM agents a
) rows
ORDER BY ord
